lead: A gear train is several gear pairs in series. Each pair changes speed and torque by its tooth ratio, and the train multiplies the ratios. An epicyclic train adds a carrier that lets one gear roll around another, so one input can give two outputs or a large reduction in a small box. Gear trains appear in a car differential, a lathe back gear, a planetary hub and a hand drill.
prereq: You need: gear nomenclature and the law of gearing from Chapter 7.1, and relative angular velocity from mechanics.

blocks.text: A gear train is a set of gears that carries motion from one shaft to another. A simple train has one gear on each shaft, so the gears mesh in one line. A compound train has at least one shaft with two gears that turn together. A reverted train is a compound train whose first and last shafts share one axis; a lathe back gear is an example.

For one pair, driver z₁ teeth drives driven z₂ teeth. The driven speed is ω₂ = −(z₁/z₂)ω₁ for external teeth; the minus sign means opposite directions. An internal pair has no minus sign. Define velocity ratio i = ω_first/ω_last. For a train, i = (z₂ z₄ …)/(z₁ z₃ …), where z₁, z₃ are drivers and z₂, z₄ are driven gears. Each external mesh reverses direction; an internal mesh does not. If i is greater than 1, the output is slower and has more torque, ignoring losses.

Example: drivers 20 and 30 teeth, driven 40 and 60 teeth. i = (40×60)/(20×30)=4, so the output turns at one quarter of the input speed. Two external meshes give no net reversal. For a reverted train with the same module, the centre distance condition is z₁+z₂ = z₃+z₄. This is the usual exam check.

An epicyclic train has a central sun gear, one or more planet gears, an internal ring gear and a carrier. The carrier pins the planets and turns about the same axis as the sun. Each planet meshes with the sun and with the ring. Constrain two members: fix one member and drive a second; the third then has one definite speed and is the output. For example, fix the ring and drive the sun, and the carrier is the output. Some syllabi call this a planetary gear train.
For a planet to touch both the sun and the ring, the tooth numbers must satisfy z_R = z_S + 2z_P. With the numbers used here, 60 = 24 + 2×18.

Do not use z_driven/z_driver directly. Hold the carrier fixed and find relative turns. Give the sun +1 turn. The planet turns −z_S/z_P because the sun-planet mesh is external. The ring turns −z_S/z_R: the planet teeth cancel, and the internal mesh keeps planet and ring in the same direction. Add c turns of the carrier to every member. The sun becomes 1+c; the ring becomes −z_S/z_R + c. If the sun is fixed, 1+c=0, so c=−1 and the ring is −(1+z_S/z_R) turns. This is the tabulation method.

blocks.where: ω_S, ω_R, ω_C are signed angular speeds of sun, ring and carrier; z_S and z_R are their tooth numbers. The right side is the speed ratio with the carrier fixed.

blocks.text: For a lossless train, T_S + T_R + T_C = 0 and T_Sω_S + T_Rω_R + T_Cω_C = 0. A fixed member has zero speed: it carries reaction torque but no power. With the sun fixed, T_R = −T_C/(1+z_S/z_R).

A car differential is epicyclic with bevel planets. The engine drives the carrier. On a straight road the planets do not spin on their pins, so both half shafts turn with the carrier. In a turn the inner wheel slows, the outer speeds up, and the average stays at carrier speed. This lets the car turn without wheel slip.

A lathe back gear is a reverted train, not epicyclic; it gives low spindle speed and high torque for heavy cuts. A planetary hub in an excavator or electric vehicle uses a small sun and several planets inside a ring, so a large reduction fits inside the wheel. The fixed ring and driven carrier give high torque at low speed. Automatic gearboxes use clutches to hold different members and select ratios; see Chapter 7.9.

figure.caption: Sun (24 teeth), planet (18 teeth), ring (60 teeth) and carrier at 100 rpm. The sun is fixed, so the ring turns at 140 rpm in the carrier's direction.

spec.aria: A graph shows a sun meshing with a planet, the planet meshing with a ring, and a carrier pinned to the planet.

examples.question: An epicyclic train has sun z_S = 24, planet z_P = 18 and ring z_R = 60. The sun is fixed. The carrier turns at 100 rpm clockwise. Find the ring speed and direction. Take clockwise as positive.
examples.answer: The ring turns at 140 rpm clockwise.
examples.check:
zs = 24
zr = 60
wc = 100.0
rel = -zs / zr
wr = wc - rel * wc
print(wr)

traps: Using z_driven/z_driver for an epicyclic train. Fix the carrier first, then add the carrier speed to every member.
Treating every mesh as a reversal. External gears reverse; an internal ring and planet keep the same direction.
Confusing planet spin with planet orbit. The planet's absolute speed is not its speed on its pin.
Forgetting the sign of a fixed member. A fixed sun has ω_S=0 exactly; this sign decides the output direction.
Using T_S+T_R+T_C=0 without signed speeds in the power equation. Power uses Tω with one sign convention.

quiz.q: Name the four members of a simple epicyclic train.
Why is z_driven/z_driver not enough for an epicyclic train?
quiz.a: The planet both spins and orbits. Speeds must be measured relative to the carrier first, then the carrier speed is added to every member.

quiz.q: A sun has z=20 and the ring has z=80. The sun is fixed and the carrier turns at 50 rpm clockwise. Find the ring speed and direction.
quiz.a: Relative ratio = −20/80 = −0.25. (ω_R−50)/(0−50)=−0.25, so ω_R−50=12.5 and ω_R=62.5 rpm clockwise.

quiz.q: A compound train has drivers of 20 and 30 teeth, driven gears of 40 and 60 teeth, two external meshes, and input 1000 rpm. Find the output speed and direction.
quiz.a: i=(40×60)/(20×30)=4. Output =1000/4=250 rpm. Two reversals cancel, so the direction is the same as the input.

quiz.q: In the worked example, fix the ring and keep the carrier at 100 rpm clockwise. Find the sun speed.
Why does a differential allow different wheel speeds while the engine drives both?
quiz.a: Its planet pinions can spin on the carrier. One half shaft slows, the other speeds up, and the carrier keeps the average speed; no wheel needs to slip.

beyond: Not for the exam. Epicyclic trains are the core of hybrid vehicle power-split devices, wind-turbine gearboxes and robot joint actuators. Engineers use the Willis equation to choose tooth numbers, then check planet bearing loads, mesh efficiency and lubrication. Search for planetary gear train Willis equation, Ravigneaux gear set, and load sharing in planetary gears to go further.
